plan: [In a second-price sealed-bid auction, truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected surplus by winning exactly when the market price (other bids) is below your value. Overbidding risks negative payoff; underbidding forgoes positive profit. Values are independent each round and no prior history is informative here. Ties are random, so bid exactly your private value to maximize long-run profit. ]

[This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. Bidding my true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit by winning exactly when the item is worth more than the highest competitor, and I pay the second-highest bid. With no history to exploit, I will bid my private value of $29.]

[This is a standard sealed-bid second-price auction with three bidders. Truthful bidding (bid = your private value) is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected payoff and avoids winning at a price above your value. No history to exploit here, so bid my value of $45 to maximize long-run profit.]
